answer: Because the wander liability is logged in the relic ledger at admission, the bridge audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 51% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind each alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 39 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
